title_original: Shared Languages: Stairway Exhibitions at The Arts Club Dubai
excerpt_original: The Arts Club Dubai’s Stairway Exhibitions returns, featuring works by two artists with distinct yet...

blocks.text: In the latest Stairway Exhibitions presented by The Arts Club Dubai , the practices of Wassef Boutros Ghali and Anthony Olubunmi Akinbola take centre stage.

The Arts Club Dubai’s Stairway Exhibitions returns, featuring works by two artists with distinct yet intersecting visual languages, taking over the first and second floors of the club in an exploration of the role of material and colour in artistic abstraction.

A collection of painted compositions by Egyptian artist Wassef Boutros Ghali is on view on the first floor, while the second floor features multimedia works by Nigerian-American artist Anthony Olubunmi Akinbola, with both presentations curated in collaboration with the club’s art advisory team at Wedel Art. Previous iterations of the exhibitions have highlighted the practices of artists such as Sarah Al Mehairi and Mandy El-Sayegh, Huguette Caland, Akram Zaatari and El Anatsui, among others.

Ajaz Sheikh, Group CEO and Partner of The Arts Club Dubai, commented: “Our Stairway Exhibitions programme has always been about bringing together important artistic voices and creating opportunities for our members to engage with art in a meaningful and personal way. With these two presentations, we bring together artists from different generations and cultural backgrounds who share an exploration of colour and abstraction, yet approach them through entirely distinct perspectives.” Through the practices of Boutros Ghali and Akinbola, patrons are urged to look beyond the surface, while pondering the ability of art to create links across time and space as new conversations surrounding form and material emerge.

blocks.caption: Anthony Olubunmi Akinbola. Installation view from Family Ties , The Arts Club Dubai, UAE, 2026. Image courtesy of The Arts Club Dubai

blocks.text: The first exhibition, Surface and Light: Works from 1970–2015, highlights Boutros Ghali’s painting practice ­– which the artist developed alongside his career as an architect – and is defined by his keen attention to detail and place. The artist moved from his home in Cairo to New York in 1969, where geometric abstraction and the Colour Field Movement were popular, and this period profoundly impacted on his work. Upon returning to Cairo in 1985, Boutros Ghali merged these artistic traditions with his own knowledge of colour and place, using the shades and energetic quality of the sunset in Egypt as a base for his creations in works such as The Blue Door (2000) and Horizon VI (2000), which are displayed in the club.

Akinbola’s expression of material and colour, also informed by a diasporic experience between Nigeria and the United States, sees the artist bring together everyday materials including hair picks, palm oil or fabric durags (scarves worn to protect hair and keep its shape). In the exhibition Family Ties , colour is expressed through these objects, most potently felt in the artist’s extensive Camouflage series (2018–ongoing), which presented over a thousand durags in an over 12-metre installation at the Queens Museum in New York City. In a recent body of work on view at The Arts Club Dubai, Akinbola pushes the durag and its material possibilities further, as the artist places the fabrics into colourful clusters recalling floral arrangements in a nod to the longstanding artistic tradition of working from nature.

In the new iteration of the Stairway Exhibitions, the artistic languages of Boutros Ghali and Akinbola meet, conveying colour through two cultural perspectives but with a concern for expressing the world that surrounds them through materials and tones deeply ingrained in their life experiences. Those with the opportunity to delve into these exhibitions at The Arts Club Dubai will surely find much to reflect upon, perhaps coming away with the conclusion that across generations and geographies, we are often the sum of our similarities rather than our differences. What does set us apart, however, can always encourage, as Sheikh notes: “[The Arts Club Dubai] is committed to encouraging curiosity, inspiring patronage and creating meaningful connections between artists, collectors and our wider community.”
Surface and Light: Works from 1970–2015 and Family Ties run until April 2027
